content:
Requirement R12 (input): Expose UAV Status. Fixed modalities: Screen and Touch. Intent: Allow the pilot to request the current status of a UAV..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-12.1, F-12.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: 2-3 distinct interaction flows, labeled Be-12.<F>.1, Be-12.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-12.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** Let the pilot obtain the current status of a selected UAV on demand (UC 5.1 / 4.2 monitoring context) — a pull-type information request, not a command that changes UAV state.

**Function candidates:**

- **F-12.1 — Pilot obtains on-demand UAV status snapshot.** Goal: pilot can pull the current attitude/health/state of a selected UAV when they choose to. Teleology = making UAV state available to the pilot at request time.

- **F-12.2 — Pilot maintains continuous awareness of active UAV status.** Goal: keep the pilot aware of the controlled UAV's status persistently (post-takeover monitoring, UC 4.2.2.13). Different goal — standing awareness vs. discrete pull.

- **F-12.3 — Pilot selects which UAV's status to expose.** Goal: in a multi-UAV team, target the status query to a specific UAV. Opens a selection/scoping goal rather than the retrieval itself.

**My steer:** R12's stated intent is "request the current status of a UAV" — a discrete pull. That's **F-12.1**. F-12.2 is a legitimately distinct standing-monitor goal but leans on a continuous data feed closer to R06/6.1 ISR-feed territory; F-12.3 is really a precondition sub-goal (selection) that other UAV requirements already touch (R09/R10 select a UAV). I'd close on **F-12.1** unless you want the persistent-monitor goal treated as its own Function here.

Which way do you want to go?

The intent of this one is just Show the tab or window or panel with the UAV's information.

.1 and .2 are the same for me and should be somethinhg like "Pilot can call out the information of any UAV connected to the aircraft and close/hide the information back when want it to"
.3 is ok

Understood — this is a display-toggle, not a data-retrieval semantics question. Merging .1/.2:

**Revised Function candidates:**

- **F-12.1 — Pilot can call up (show) and dismiss (hide) the status panel of any connected UAV.** Goal: control the visibility of the UAV information surface on demand — open it when wanted, close it back when done. Toggle of a panel/tab/window.

- **F-12.3 — Pilot selects which connected UAV's status the panel exposes.** Goal: in a multi-UAV team, scope the shown information to a specific UAV.

Note F-12.1 and F-12.3 are tightly coupled (you pick a UAV, then its panel shows), but they're distinct goals: one governs *visibility of the surface*, the other governs *whose data fills it*. Both are legitimate to keep.

Given your stated intent ("just show the tab/window/panel"), I'd close on **F-12.1** as the primary Function for R12, and treat F-12.3 as a supporting selection goal only if you want the multi-UAV scoping designed here rather than inherited from the R09/R10 selection pattern.

Close on F-12.1 alone, or keep F-12.3 in scope too?

Closing Function layer: **F-12.1 — Pilot can call up (show) and dismiss (hide) the status panel of any connected UAV.**

**Behaviour candidates (Screen + Touch):**

- **Be-12.1.1 — Toggle affordance (open/close on same control).** A persistent UAV-status control (button/tab). Tap → panel appears with current status; tap again → panel hides. Single reused affordance drives both directions. Modality-complete: Touch tap or bezel OSS both toggle; Screen renders the panel.

- **Be-12.1.2 — Separate show / dismiss affordances.** One control opens the panel; a distinct close control (X on the panel, or dismiss OSS) hides it. Explicit two-action model — no ambiguity about current state, but two surfaces to maintain.

- **Be-12.1.3 — Auto-surface on connect, manual dismiss/recall.** Panel auto-appears when a UAV connection is established (ties to R10 takeover completion, UC 4.2.2.12), pilot can hide it and recall it later via the status control. Couples visibility to connection state rather than being purely pilot-initiated.

**My steer:** Your intent is a clean pilot-driven show/hide. **Be-12.1.1** (toggle) is the tightest match — one affordance, minimal cockpit real estate, lowest workload in a high-load environment. Be-12.1.2 adds robustness (state always unambiguous) but costs a second control; Be-12.1.3 overreaches into auto-behaviour that belongs more to R10's completion notification than to this pull-panel.

One flag: whichever toggle affordance we pick is a strong **reuse candidate** — the R10 takeover-complete flow and R11 acknowledgments already surface UAV info; this status panel is likely the *same* WAD panel those reference, just made pilot-toggleable.

Lean Be-12.1.1?

.1 and .2 can be both applied.
.3 I think is not good

Agreed — drop Be-12.1.3 (auto-surface belongs to R10's completion flow, not here).

Combining .1 and .2: the panel is **opened by a toggle/status control and can be closed either by re-pressing that same control or via a dedicated close affordance on the panel itself**. Toggle for economy, explicit X for unambiguous dismissal — they coexist without conflict.

**Closing Behaviour layer: Be-12.1.1 + Be-12.1.2 (combined)** — Pilot shows the UAV status panel via a persistent status control; hides it by re-pressing that control *or* using a dedicated close affordance on the panel. Modality-complete: Touch (tap control / tap X) or Keyboard (bezel OSS toggle / dismiss OSS); Screen renders the panel.

Moving to Structure.

**Structure candidates (S-12.1.[1+2]):**

- **S-12.1.[1+2].1 — Reused UAV Detail Panel + status tab.** The same WAD UAV detail/status panel referenced by R10/R11, now with a persistent **UAV Status tab/OSS** to toggle it and a **close (X) control** on the panel header. Panel body renders attitude/health/state (Screen). Toggle tab = Touch or bezel OSS; X = Touch or dismiss OSS. Maximal reuse — no new panel, just makes the existing one pilot-toggleable.

- **S-12.1.[1+2].2 — Dedicated standalone Status window (overlay layer).** A new stacked WAD overlay window, invoked by a dedicated **STATUS** button (WAD + bezel OSS), with its own header/close. Independent of R10/R11 panels. More real estate flexibility, but duplicates a surface that likely already exists.

- **S-12.1.[1+2].3 — HUD status flag + WAD panel pair.** WAD panel as above, plus a compact persistent **HUD status line** always showing connected-UAV summary; WAD panel is the full toggleable detail. Splits summary (always-on HUD) from detail (toggled WAD).

**My steer:** **S-12.1.[1+2].1** — reuse the existing UAV detail panel from R10/R11 rather than build a parallel surface. Add the status tab/OSS (toggle) and header X (dismiss), satisfying both combined behaviours with modality completeness. S-12.1.[1+2].3's HUD flag conflicts with your "just show the panel on demand" intent (it makes status always-on). S-12.1.[1+2].2 needlessly duplicates.

Lean S-12.1.[1+2].1?
I think only the first one.

Confirmed. Closing Structure layer on **S-12.1.[1+2].1** — reused WAD UAV Detail/Status Panel (shared with R10/R11), with a persistent **UAV Status tab/OSS** (toggle show/hide) and a **header close (X)** control; panel body renders attitude/health/state. Modality-complete: Touch (tab / X) or Keyboard (bezel toggle OSS / dismiss OSS); Screen renders the panel.

**R12 summary:**
- **F-12.1** — Pilot can call up and dismiss the status panel of any connected UAV.
- **Be-12.1.1 + Be-12.1.2** (combined) — Show via persistent status control; hide via re-press *or* dedicated close affordance. Modality-complete.
- **S-12.1.[1+2].1** — Reused WAD UAV Detail/Status Panel + status tab/OSS + header X. Shared with R10/R11.

R12 ready to close. Confirm to finalize, or revisit any layer.
